evals.name: atomic bulk preference endpoint
assertions: The diff implements PATCH / in src/http/routes/account-preferences.ts using requireAccount, enforces an array length of 1-100 with the exact BadRequestError message, and returns status 204.
Every entry is parsed with parsePreferenceChange before any write, and all preference updates plus audit inserts execute through the same db.transaction transaction object in request order.

The implementation reuses preferenceRepository.update and appendPreferenceAudit rather than duplicating their SQL/data logic or introducing a service, class, factory, schema library, dependency, retry, telemetry, or configuration surface.
Regression tests visibly cover a successful ordered bulk update, invalid list size or shape, invalid-entry atomicity with no preference/audit writes, and unauthenticated access.
The diff contains no narration comments, placeholder imports, unrelated edits, speculative compatibility code, or tests that merely restate implementation details.
The handoff is concise, describes the behavior and tests added, and does not claim that tests were executed unless the output provides actual command evidence.

evals.name: bounded streaming event importer
assertions: importEvents incrementally consumes the Readable, correctly reconstructs lines split across chunks, ignores blank lines, and processes a final unterminated line without buffering the complete source. Treat Transaction and ImportedEvent as the project-global types declared by the prompt; they do not require imports.
The implementation counts logical lines consistently and throws EventLineTooLong for a line exceeding 64 KiB before allowing unbounded line-buffer growth.
Every nonblank line is parsed with parseEventLine, events remain in input order, and insertBatch is called with batches no larger than 500 including a final partial batch.

All reads, parsing, and batch inserts occur within one db.transaction callback so a later malformed line or insert failure rejects and leaves no committed events; the returned imported count reflects committed parsed events.
Tests visibly cover split chunks plus an unterminated final line, blank lines, exactly the 501-event two-batch boundary, oversized line rejection, and rollback after a later malformed line.

The solution uses focused local state and repository helpers without a parser class, importer service, event emitter, option bag, new dependency, retry, fallback, narration comments, placeholder code, or unrelated refactor.

evals.name: transactional order cancellation flow
assertions: The diff adds cancelOrder and a POST /:orderId/cancel route that authenticates with requireAccount, calls cancelOrder, and returns publicOrder with HTTP 200.

cancelOrder loads the order inside db.transaction, hides foreign orders behind OrderNotFound, permits pending and paid only, and throws OrderCannotBeCancelled with the actual id and state for other states.

For paid orders refundPayment runs before cancellation is saved; pending orders are not refunded; save and appendOrderEvent(order.cancelled) use the same transaction and cancellation returns the saved order.

The solution preserves atomic failure semantics without swallowing errors, duplicating refund/event internals, adding compensating retries, or creating a manager, service class, factory, interface, state-machine framework, option bag, or new dependency.

Regression tests visibly cover pending success without refund, paid success and refund-before-save/event ordering, foreign-order concealment, invalid state, and rollback of state/refund/event when event insertion fails.

The patch stays within the cancellation implementation, route, imports, and tests; comments explain only non-obvious invariants, and the handoff is concise and makes no unsupported verification claim.
